---
title: "PEVmax"
description: "PEVmax is the largest prediction error variance among the test individuals, so it protects the worst-predicted one."
---

PEVmax is the largest prediction error variance among the test individuals, so it protects the worst-predicted one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Model-based |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | yes |
| Score a given set | `pevmax_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "PEVmax")` |

## Definition

$\mathrm{PEVmax} = \max_i x_{0i}' B x_{0i}$ with an intercept column and $B = (X'X + \lambda I)^{-1}$. Without a test set the candidates left out of the training set are the target.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
pevmax_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "PEVmax",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "PEVmax", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Akdemir, D., Sanchez, J. I., & Jannink, J.-L. (2015). Optimization of genomic selection training populations with a genetic algorithm. *Genetics Selection Evolution, 47*, 38. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12711-015-0116-6>

Isidro y Sánchez, J., & Akdemir, D. (2021). Training set optimization for sparse phenotyping in genomic selection: a conceptual overview. *Frontiers in Plant Science, 12*, 715910. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2021.715910>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** R package STPGA by Akdemir and colleagues: [CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA) (GPL-3).
